message.content:
**Uno – Quick‑Start Rules** | Step | What Happens | Key Points | |------|--------------|------------| | **1. Setup** | • Shuffle the Uno deck (108 cards).
• Deal 7 cards to each player.
• Place the remaining cards face‑down as the draw pile.
• Flip the top card of the draw pile to start the discard pile. | • If the first card is an action card, its effect applies to the first player. | | **2. Turn Order** | • Players take turns clockwise (or counterclockwise if a “Reverse” card is played). | • The goal is to get rid of all your cards. | | **3. Playing a Card** | • On your turn, you may play one card that matches the **color**, **number**, or **symbol** of the top discard card.
• If you have no playable card, you must draw one from the draw pile. | • If the drawn card is playable, you may play it immediately. | | **4. Action Cards** | • **Skip** – next player loses their turn.
• **Reverse** – changes direction of play.
• **Draw Two** – next player draws two cards and skips their turn.
• **Wild** – you choose the new color.
• **Wild Draw Four** – you choose the new color; next player draws four cards and skips their turn (only playable if you have no matching color). | • “Wild Draw Four” can be challenged if the opponent believes you had a playable card. | | **5. Calling “Uno”** | • When you play your second‑to‑last card, shout “UNO!” before the next player takes their turn.
• Failure to call “UNO” when required results in a penalty: draw two cards. | • If you’re caught calling “UNO” too early (when you still have more than two cards), you also draw two cards. | | **6. Winning a Round** | • The round ends when a player discards their last card.
• Score points: number cards = face value, Draw Two/Reverse/Skip = 20, Wild/Wild Draw Four = 50. | • The winner of the round gets the points from all other players’ remaining cards. | | **7. Game End** | • Play continues until a player reaches a predetermined score (commonly 500). | • The player with the lowest score at the end wins. | --- ### Quick Tips - **Keep track of colors** – If you’re out of a particular color, try to hold onto a Wild card for flexibility. - **Watch the discard pile** – Knowing what’s been played helps you anticipate opponents’ moves. - **Use “Wild Draw Four” wisely** – It’s powerful but risky; use it when you’re sure you have no matching color. Enjoy the fast‑paced, colorful fun of Uno!
